Both candidates were rendered by patching a literal colour into the pane; the real change must refit code_selection_background in the palettes, which is a different diff from the one that produced these pixels.

subjects.description: A solid selection band with a white foreground, the way ordinary text selection works. Reaches the contrast requirement with certainty and needs no painting work. The cost is that the syntax colouring of the selected line is replaced while it is selected, on the one line the reviewer is most likely studying.

subjects.description: A heavier translucent wash in a saturated colour. Clears the requirement while leaving some of the underlying line visible through it. Syntax colouring survives but is tinted, which may read as a different colour rather than as the same colour under a highlight.

detail_sections.heading: What was ruled out and why
items: Keeping alpha 72 and only refitting the palette: capped at 2.01:1 by the alpha, so it cannot reach 3:1 with any colour.
Opaque band keeping the current #d8e9ff: 1.23:1, because that colour is too pale even fully opaque.
Translucent wash plus a full-opacity underline: QTextCharFormat underline is not drawn for a full-width ExtraSelection, so this mechanism does not exist.

A painted left-margin bar: needs viewport-margin painting, which perturbs the pane geometry RFC-BPR-0005's measured axis and bounded-widget counts rest on. Not rendered here; say so if you want it costed.

Tinted syntax colours may be misread as different token categories
